3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 3

Have got / has got

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use have got and has got to talk about possessions and appearance
  • Make negative sentences with haven't got and hasn't got
  • Ask questions with Have you got…? / Has she got…? and give short answers
  • Describe people and monsters: hair, eyes and body parts

Para pensar

Tu amigo dice «I've got a dog» y su hermana dice «She's got a cat». ¿Por qué una vez es «have» y otra «has»?

Explicación

What does have got mean?

We use have got to say what we have: things («I've got a new bike»), family and pets («I've got two cats») and parts of our body or appearance («I've got brown eyes»).

En castellano: have got significa «tener». Ojo: no sirve para la edad. En español «tengo ocho años», pero en inglés es «I am eight». Tampoco se usa para el hambre o el frío: «I'm hungry», «I'm cold».

Have got or has got?

The verb changes with the person. With I, you, we, they we use have got: «I have got», «They have got». With he, she, it we use has got: «He has got», «My sister has got», «The dog has got».

In speaking we use short forms: I've got, you've got, we've got, they've got; he's got, she's got, it's got. Truco: si puedes cambiar el sujeto por he, she o it, usa has: «Pablo (he) has got a ball».

The negative: haven't got, hasn't got

To say that you do not have something, add not: haven't got (have not got) and hasn't got (has not got). «I haven't got a sister.» «My cat hasn't got a long tail.»

We often join a positive and a negative sentence with but: «I've got a brother, but I haven't got a sister.» «She's got a scooter, but she hasn't got a bike.» En castellano: en español basta con «no tengo»; en inglés el not va pegado a have o has.

Questions: Have you got…?

To ask, put Have or Has at the beginning: «Have you got a pet?», «Has your dad got a car?», «Have they got a garden?». Got stays in the middle.

Short answers repeat have or has, without got: «Yes, I have.» / «No, I haven't.» «Yes, he has.» / «No, he hasn't.» Ojo: no contestes «Yes, I have got»: es demasiado largo y suena raro.

Describing people: hair and eyes

We use have got to describe people. Hair can be long or short, straight (liso), curly (rizado) or wavy (ondulado), and blond (rubio), brown (castaño), black, red (pelirrojo) or grey. Eyes can be blue, green, brown or black.

«She's got long curly red hair and green eyes.» Ojo al orden: en inglés el adjetivo va delante: «long hair», no «hair long». Y hair no lleva -s: «He's got short hair».

Body parts

To describe animals and monsters, we need the parts of the body: head (cabeza), eyes (ojos), ears (orejas), nose (nariz), mouth (boca), teeth (dientes), arms (brazos), hands (manos), legs (piernas), feet (pies) and, for animals, tail (cola), wings (alas) and fur (pelo de animal).

Plurales especiales: one foot → two feet; one tooth → many teeth. «An elephant has got big ears and a long nose (trunk).»

Meet the monsters!

Read about two monsters. «Blip is green. It's got three eyes, four arms and two long antennae. It hasn't got any hair. It's got sharp teeth, but it's very friendly!» «Zuzu is purple. It's got one big eye, two short legs and a long tail. It hasn't got any arms.»

Answer: Has Blip got any hair? How many eyes has Zuzu got? En castellano: para animales y cosas usamos it, por eso es it's got.

Possessions: my favourite things

We also use have got for our possessions (things we own): toys, clothes, school things. «I've got a skateboard, a tablet and lots of books.» «My best friend has got a big collection of stickers.»

Use a before a consonant sound (a ball, a kite) and an before a vowel sound (an apple, an umbrella, an orange T-shirt). For plurals, use a number or some: «I've got three balls», «She's got some crayons».

Let's practise: draw a monster

Play Monster dictation in pairs. Draw a secret monster. Don't show it! Describe it to your partner: «My monster has got two heads. It's got four eyes on each head. It hasn't got any legs, but it's got wings.» Your partner draws it.

Then compare the drawings. Are they similar? Now swap. Your partner can ask questions: «Has it got a tail?» — «Yes, it has. A long blue tail.» ¡Gana la pareja cuyo dibujo se parezca más!

Have got y has got

Ejercicios

  1. Completa: «I ___ got a cat.»

  2. Completa: «She ___ got curly hair.»

  3. Escribe en negativa: «We've got a garden.»

  4. Escribe en negativa: «He's got a bike.»

  5. Pregunta: «they / a dog»

  6. Respuesta corta: «Has your mum got a car?» (no)

  7. Traduce: pelo rizado, ojos verdes.

  8. ¿Cuál es el plural de foot y de tooth?

  9. ¿A o an? «___ umbrella», «___ kite».

  10. Describe a un compañero con dos frases.

Practica

  1. «Tener» in English is…

    1. A) be
    2. B) have got
    3. C) do

  2. My sister ___ got a scooter.

    1. A) has
    2. B) have
    3. C) is

  3. We ___ got a big garden.

    1. A) has
    2. B) are
    3. C) have

  4. «He's got» means…

    1. A) he is got
    2. B) he was got
    3. C) he has got

  5. I ___ got a brother.

    1. A) haven't
    2. B) hasn't
    3. C) don't

  6. «Have you got a pet?» — «Yes, …»

    1. A) I have got.
    2. B) I have.
    3. C) I am.

  7. ___ your dad got a car?

    1. A) Has
    2. B) Have
    3. C) Is

  8. «Pelo rizado» is…

    1. A) hair curly
    2. B) curly hairs
    3. C) curly hair

  9. One foot, two…

    1. A) foots
    2. B) feet
    3. C) feets

  10. I've got ___ apple.

    1. A) a
    2. B) an
    3. C) two

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve have got; Cuándo se usa have y cuándo has; Cómo se hacen la negativa y la pregunta; Cómo describo a una persona o a un monstruo.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

have gotTener (I, you, we, they).
has gotTener (he, she, it).
I've got / she's gotFormas cortas.
haven't got / hasn't gotNo tener.
Have you got…?¿Tienes…? → Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
curly / straightRizado / liso.
feet / teethPies / dientes (plurales especiales).
a / anan delante de vocal: an apple.

Soluciones

  1. B) Have got.
  2. A) She → has.
  3. C) We → have.
  4. C) 's = has.
  5. A) I → haven't.
  6. B) Respuesta corta.
  7. A) Your dad → has.
  8. C) Adjetivo delante.
  9. B) Plural irregular.
  10. B) Vocal: an.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. have (I've got).
  2. has (she's got).
  3. We haven't got a garden.
  4. He hasn't got a bike.
  5. Have they got a dog?
  6. No, she hasn't.
  7. curly hair, green eyes.
  8. feet y teeth.
  9. an umbrella, a kite.
  10. Model answer: Marta has got long brown hair. She's got brown eyes.
